quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look far ahead down the road.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead down the road.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead to spot dangers early. This gives you time to react before a problem occurs.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve separately, one after the other. Never brake while swerving because it can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign appears on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Need less space to stop than larger vehicles.
Need the same space to stop as larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need the same space to stop as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance between you and other vehicles. Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign tells you a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a problem?

options.text: Changes in the road surface ahead
Road conditions that stay the same

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions that stay the same
questions.explanation: Watch for changes in road conditions and traffic. Plan how to handle them safely.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Be loose enough to let wind blow through.
Fit snug so they don't flap in the wind.
Be so tight you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snug so they don't flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should fit snugly to stop flapping, but still loose enough to move your body.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Full-fingered gloves give you a better grip and protect your hands. Choose gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This is safest because it keeps distance from both the passing driver and traffic in other lanes.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should riders arrange themselves?
questions.explanation: A staggered pattern is best for groups. It keeps riders close together while giving each person enough space to stop safely. Use single-file only when turning, entering a highway, or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how long does it take a motorcycle to stop and speed up?

options.text: The same amount of time as usual.

questions.explanation: Extra weight slows a motorcycle down. It takes longer to speed up and stop with a passenger than it does alone. Your motorcycle will respond more slowly to your commands.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane helps a car driver see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind can prevent side mirror use.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.

questions.question: How should you position your arms when holding the motorcycle handlebars?
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to hazards.
You have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react and maneuver if another vehicle makes a mistake. This does not help you accelerate faster into a curve.

questions.question: Where is there the most risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles is greatest at intersections.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, what must you do?
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, you must shift into higher gears.

questions.question: When is there less traction available for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, such as in a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop, when you cannot see clearly, or when traffic is heavy. Bad weather like rain makes it harder to stop quickly.

questions.question: What can happen if you grab the front brake hard or jam the rear brake?

options.text: It is the best way to stop in an emergency.
It is the best way to slow down when streets are wet.

questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or jamming the rear brake can cause the brakes to lock. This makes it hard to control your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is a sign that your rear tire has gone flat?

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
You see air coming out of the tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
questions.explanation: When the rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle may jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, should you move to the far edge of your lane?

options.text: Yes, because you will be farther away from the passing vehicle.
No, because it may cause the other driver to move back too soon.
It does not matter because it has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it may cause the other driver to move back too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far edge of your lane when being passed. This may make the passing driver move back into your lane too early and create a danger.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.
